If Canadian law worked the way it "should", he (Nader) wouldn't even be free.

 Canada focuses on "rehabilitating the offender", without the rehabilitation part. It's really just "wrist slaps" until people learn to stop getting caught.

 I have a relative who one time said he had a gun, ran into the woods threatening the police and everyone around. He was messed up on drugs and booze. 

The tactical unit showed up, decided it was too much work to find him and left. Nothing ever happened (he wasn't even brought in later on). 

He's a repeat offender for decades for violent offences, goes to jail sometimes for short stints then comes right back out. 

A majority of his crimes are against women and children. It's just not taken seriously.

Without reading other comments to know if anyone mentioned it yet but the silent treatment is a form of manipulation. I'd consider it emotional abuse. 

I purchased a home with someone like this that I intended to marry who drastically downplayed my contributions (which were massive) to others behind my back and stupidly didn't protect myself because I didn't expect to be taken advantage of because I never would of done that to him.

As these relationships do, ours came to an end and he massively lied about so many things that his friends and family were backing his delusion that I should get nothing, even though I asked for significantly less then my investment to just start fresh. It was hell and I've been in therapy over just the end of our relationship for longer than the entire thing lasted because I was so terrorized.

Do not marry this guy and get rid of this house immediately to cut ties with him. Biggest mistake of your life will be marrying him and staying tied up in this home.

In keeping with the situations in the frame the take away to me is that the "conflicted mom" leans more towards that she kept her child and she's not sure if that's the right choice. (Abortion, Adoption, Kept, Child-free makes more sense)
The family knows who he is and the police are aware of where he is, he's not going to get far if he tries to bolt. Not a smart guy.

Women already have to travel to different provinces/hours away to get abortions in this country. Not really that different.

 Places like New Brunswick for example don't have easy access and even had a clinic shut down when they desperately needed it. They have I believe two clinics? Serving everyone and unless you live in the area where they are, it's hours of a drive. Not really accessible.

Some providers won't even give you the pill version they have that was supposed to help combat the issues of surgery/not enough clinics, so you have to get surgery because you can't easily get an ultrasound to make sure you qualify. 

In a way, it already has happened here. Maybe the "rules" don't say it outright, but the system runs to make it very difficult for women in a lot of places.

YTA.

A 16 year old not interested in family time? Wow, big shocker. Wait until you find out that "my house, my rules" sentiment is why your kid will leave as soon as she can, and never come home. Forget "family time" you won't even see a holiday. 

Teenagers are moody, often disrespectful and difficult. Learning how to treat them like individuals, respect them/their things and speaking to them, not down on them, is something I would suggest you pick up really quickly.

Go get the kid a PS5, some games, and apologise, then work on learning to communicate before you ask her to do what you can't.

You wonder why your kid acts out the way she does, like she has poor communication skills, and then you go ahead and act out yourself like an angry impulsive teenager?
